correctness.rationale: Direct 2x2 inversion gives R_B=q_B(mean)/scatter+B11/m with no approximation. An orthogonal decomposition of m input sites has Jacobian sqrt(m) and residual dimension m-1; after rescaling the event ball, bounded continuous density and compact support justify dominated convergence to the exact tube-volume coefficient. The strictly positive coefficient and layer-cake identity give exactly the negative-moment frontier. Holder inequality with its equality characterization establishes the unique positive continuous minimizer. The package includes a standalone verifier that passed 1,528 exact-rational and numerical checks; those are corroborative, not the proof of infinite limits.

originality.rationale: The principal comparison is to randomized least-squares point selection, generic sample covariance lower-tail theory, and mixed volume/importance sampling experimental designs. The retrieved full texts establish different guarantees rather than an exact unweighted two-parameter iid inverse-information risk tail and a unique continuous density minimizing its leading coefficient for all sample sizes. Related prior results on beta-node affine slope moment thresholds already cover some moment-existence special cases, and unit-vector random-angle observability has a matching exponent, but neither yields the present variable-norm affine loss-weighted coefficient or its universal density optimizer. This is a best-knowledge publication-priority assessment, not an assertion of global uniqueness of the claim.

value.rationale: The object is the naturally occurring inverse information risk of the smallest nontrivial unweighted iid affine least-squares model. The exact asymptotic tail quantifies catastrophic failures missed by mean or typical condition numbers, and the unique design density has a non-obvious invariance across every sample size. For four draws over [-10,10] with Euclidean coefficient loss, the uniform-design leading tail constant is 6.943939 times the optimum. This is a motivated full classification of a practical rare-event design criterion, not a routine parameter substitution or arbitrary finite slice.
